newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Forex dealers warned of possible job threat.
newsitem.headline: Forex dealers warned of possible job threat.

text.p: Amid praise for Asia's stunning growth as a financial centre, a convention of foreign exchange dealers here ended on a sombre note as dealers were warned their jobs could come under increasing threat.
"I am scared for our industry," said Chris Pavlou, Treasurer at HSBC Midland Bank Plc in Tokyo and Asia-Pacific Executive of the Association Cambiste Internationale (ACI).
The dealers were in Manila for a conference of Asia-Pacific forex dealers, which ended on Friday.
Speaking at the end of the two-day Asia Pacific Forex Assembly, Pavlou noted that in a recent industry newsletter, three out of four headlines spoke of banks cutting jobs.
"It is an issue that we face as an industry, and history will look at us as arrogant, irresponsible people if we didn't stop and take a look at it," he added.

Pavlou attributed the situation mainly to lower gross profits among banks as a whole and high overheads, but added that general workplace insecurity, promoted partly by a disappearance of the teamwork ethic, also had taken a toll.

He cited rising costs in particular, noting that recent financial mishaps have boosted management demands for expensive risk management personnel, while demands for increasingly fast information access have led to a dependence on highly specialised and costlly technology.
"About 70 percent of this (technology) is unnecessary," he said.

But Pavlou also praised the strides taken by the host country, the Philippines, saying: "Five years ago, this country was treated with skepticism....but now it is an example of what a developing country can do. We have a success story to tell."

His words echoed those of Philippine President Fidel Ramos, the keynote speaker on Thursday, who said: "We have turned our economic situation from decline to growth, and now we believe we are on the threshold of economic growth equal to that of our Asian neighbours."
The Philippines' next chance to shine on a world stage comes when leaders of the 18-member Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation gather on November 25.
